before.best_for: AI search, deep research, agentic computer control, finance and study tools
before.description: Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine that returns cited, up-to-date sources instead of a list of links, with an agentic Deep Research mode and multi-model access to systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other vendors.
before.description_long:
Perplexity is a conversational search tool that answers questions with cited, up-to-date sources instead of a list of links. It sits somewhere between a chatbot and a search engine, and it has leaned hard into research and agentic work.

The headline feature is Advanced Deep Research. It runs agentically inside Perplexity's Computer assistant, asks clarifying questions before it starts, accepts follow-ups mid-run, and shows live source and progress tracking.

Beyond research, Perplexity gives you multi-model access to systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other vendors, plus the Comet browser for AI-assisted browsing.

Pricing is tiered. Free costs $0 a month. Pro costs $20 a month or $200 a year billed annually, and includes 4,000 bonus Computer credits; Perplexity's own pricing page shows the annual plan's per-month equivalent as $17. Max costs $200 a month or $2,000 a year billed annually, shown as an annual-equivalent $167 a month, and includes 10,000 monthly Computer credits plus 35,000 bonus credits. Enterprise Pro costs $40 per seat per month or $400 per seat per year (education/nonprofit pricing is lower), and Enterprise Max costs $325 per seat per month or $3,250 per seat per year. An Education Pro plan is available at $10 a month with SheerID student verification.

The limitations are worth knowing. Like any AI system it can still misread or over-trust weak sources, so citations need checking. The free tier is limited for frequent use, and agentic Computer work is metered by a monthly credit budget that heavy users can exhaust. Juggling multiple models also adds a learning curve for some users.

Perplexity is a strong pick if you do a lot of source-backed research, want agentic Deep Research, or like having access to several AI models in one subscription. Casual users who just need a few answers a day can stay on Free, while heavier users can choose either monthly or annual billing on Pro or Max.
pros: Advanced Deep Research is genuinely agentic: it asks clarifying questions, takes mid-run follow-ups, and shows live sources and progress
Answers come with inline citations, making them easier to verify than a plain chatbot reply
Multi-model access to systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other vendors
Both Pro and Max are available on monthly billing ($20/month and $200/month) as well as annual billing, so you are not forced into a yearly commitment
A genuine free tier exists for occasional use at no cost
cons: Like all AI tools it can still misread or over-trust weak sources, so citations need a second look
Free tier is limited for people who search frequently
Max costs $200/month ($2,000/year), a steep step up from Pro's $20/month ($200/year)
Agentic Computer work is metered by monthly credits, which heavy users can exhaust
Multiple models and the Comet browser add complexity for people who just want a quick answer
choose_if: You do frequent research and want answers backed by live, checkable sources
You want agentic Deep Research with clarifying questions and live progress tracking
You want access to multiple AI models from different vendors in one subscription
You need the highest usage limits and priority access and are comfortable with Max's $200/month or $2,000/year price

faq.a: Perplexity searches the web including academic sources, but it doesn't specialize in peer-reviewed papers the way Consensus does. For academic research requiring study citations and evidence quality, Consensus is more reliable. Perplexity is better for broad current-events research.
faq.q: Is Perplexity good for academic research?
